text: Before close assault on a defended position: fire_barrage with SP >= half of defending SP to pin and attrit, then close_assault with 3:1 or better ratio. Never assault at less than 2:1.
Water resupply sequence: truck_attach to the thirsty unit, truck_load water from a port or supply dump, truck_unload at the target unit. draw_water ONLY works on oasis/bir terrain.
Fuel resupply: truck_attach to motorized unit, truck_load fuel from port or dump, truck_unload. Motorized units consume fuel per CPA spent moving. Keep fuel above 50% before advancing.
Allied attacker must advance every turn toward the next objective. Stalling loses VP. If no assault is possible, at minimum move units closer to the next objective hex.

Axis defender should hold objective hexes and only withdraw when facing 3:1+ odds. A unit destroyed in place costs 0.5 VP per SP but holding the hex denies the Allied player objective VP which is worth more.
Never attack with isolated units. Mass 3+ units adjacent to the target hex before assaulting. Piecemeal attacks waste SP and give the defender counterattack opportunities.
After the enemy assaults and is weakened (lost SP), counterattack with close_assault if you have local superiority. Damaged units after assault are vulnerable.
After a successful close_assault, immediately move_unit into the captured hex and continue advancing toward the next enemy position. Do not pause after victory — pursue.
Create supply dumps 2-3 hexes behind the front line, not on front-line hexes where they can be captured. Dumps at ports are safe but far from the front.
Allied fleet sorties should target enemy coastal positions to soften them before ground assault. Time fleet sorties to the same turn as your planned ground attack.
Axis convoys must deliver enough tonnage each turn to sustain the front. Plan convoy tonnage to match expected consumption. Monitor losses and adjust routing.
Use air recon missions on hexes where enemy presence is suspected but not confirmed. Knowing enemy positions is essential before committing to attack.
Retreat when: facing 3:1+ odds with no reinforcements coming, supply is critical and no resupply possible, or position is flanked with risk of encirclement. Otherwise HOLD.
Attack sequence: 1) barrage to pin/attrit, 2) anti_armor against armored defenders, 3) close_assault with massed infantry at 3:1+. Skipping barrage wastes assault SP.
Victory points: objectives (Sidi Barrani 3VP, Bardia 3VP, Tobruk 5VP, Alexandria 5VP) plus 0.5 VP per enemy SP destroyed. 5+ margin = marginal victory, 15+ = decisive. Track VP every turn.
Assign 1-2 fighters to OCAP over the front line. OCAP fighters auto-intercept enemy sorties within 6 hexes. Place OCAP at forward airfields closest to the front.
Keep at least 1 fighter on DCAP at each operational SGSU. DCAP screens all aircraft at the base from enemy attack. Without DCAP, enemy bombers can hit your parked aircraft.
Concentrate bombing sorties on a single hex rather than spreading across multiple targets. Mass bombardment at one point causes more disruption than scattered bombing.
Use fighters with tacair for strafing missions against enemy trucks and supply dumps. Destroying supply infrastructure is more valuable long-term than hitting combat units.
Always fly recon before committing bombers. Non-recon missions against un-sighted hexes risk semi-sighted abort (must roll to proceed). Recon sights the hex for subsequent missions.
When outnumbered in the air, conserve fighters for DCAP defense. Only fly offensive missions with fighters when you have 3+ ready. Losing fighters degrades all future air operations.
Experienced pilots provide +2 maneuver per experience level in air combat. Protect aces by assigning them to OCAP rather than risky ground attack missions.
With air superiority (2:1+ aircraft ratio), fly aggressive bombing and strafing against enemy concentrations. Use recon freely. Assign minimal DCAP. Enemy can't challenge your missions.
Under air inferiority, assign all fighters to DCAP to protect bases. Fly only essential recon with your fastest aircraft. Avoid bombing missions — losing bombers is permanent.
Check aircraft range before assigning missions. Effective range is half the type's range_hexes (round trip). Gladiators from Matruh cannot reach Benghazi. Use forward SGSUs for deep strikes.
Enemy hexes with heavy flak units are dangerous for low-level strafing. Bombers face light flak everywhere. Avoid strafing hexes with known gun units — use bombing instead.
RAF has fewer but better fighters (Hurricane I maneuver 34 vs CR.42 at 26). Use Hurricanes for OCAP to dominate air combat. Assign Gladiators to DCAP or recon. Send Blenheims for bombing.

Regia Aeronautica has quantity: 12 squadrons. CR.42 fighters are outclassed by Hurricanes but adequate against Gladiators. Mass SM.79 bombers against Allied positions. Use fighters to protect bomber formations.
Luftwaffe arrives GT25 with Bf.109E (maneuver 38) and Ju.87 Stukas, then GT27 with Bf.110 and Ju.88. These aircraft outclass all RAF types. Upon arrival, shift to aggressive air superiority stance.
When ground units are in contact with the enemy, prioritize ground support: bomb enemy-held hexes adjacent to your units. Bombardment reduces defender strength before close assault, improving odds.
Route Axis convoys to the port closest to the front line. Tobruk is 5 tons/turn but saves 20+ hexes of trucking vs Tripoli. Benghazi is the best compromise: decent capacity and moderate distance.
Plan convoy tonnage to match consumption rate. Each combat unit burns ~2 tons/turn of mixed supply. An offensive requires 50% more than sustaining defense. Shortfall cascades within 2-3 turns.
Assign at least 1 fighter to convoy CAP when enemy fleet has sortied recently. CAP reduces interception threshold by 1 on the d6 roll. Without CAP, convoys face full interception odds.
Allied fleet has 2 sorties per turn. Use fleet_sortie to interdict Axis convoys. Time sorties when Axis plans large tonnage shipments — intercepting 40 tons hurts more than intercepting 10.
After a fleet engagement, the fleet needs 3 turns to repair. Don't sortie every turn — save sorties for critical moments when Axis convoys carry maximum tonnage or when preparing your own offensive.
Unload at forward ports first to minimize truck distance. Supply distribution from convoys: 35% fuel, 30% ammo, 20% stores, 15% water. Match unloading to the most critical shortage.
Fly recon over convoy lanes before fleet sortie. Reconned lanes give +1 to interception roll (threshold becomes 4 instead of 3). Combined with fleet sortie, this maximizes convoy disruption.
After convoy losses, immediately plan replacement tonnage next turn. Don't let supply shortfall compound. If interception destroyed 30%+, consider rerouting to a safer port even if farther.
Capturing a forward port (Tobruk, Bardia) dramatically shortens supply lines. Prioritize port hexes as offensive objectives. A captured port operational within 1 turn changes the logistics game.
Monitor supply pool levels every turn. When fuel drops below 500 tons, prioritize fuel convoys. When water drops below 500 tons, water becomes critical. Never let both run low simultaneously.

Use fleet sorties against coastal positions to soften defenses before ground assault. Fleet bombardment at half strength still adds firepower. Coordinate fleet sortie timing with the ground offensive turn.
Axis coastal shipping moves supplies between Tripoli and forward ports. Shorter routes are safer from interception. When Allied fleet is under repair, ship maximum tonnage through all lanes.

CRITICAL: When retreating, ALWAYS retreat along the coast road (B3010->B3610->B4010->B4210->B4810->B5010). These hexes have ports with water. NEVER retreat into interior desert hexes — units at zero water lose 1 SP per turn and will be destroyed by dehydration, not combat.

After destroying enemy forward units, do NOT stop advancing. Continue moving toward objective hexes: Sidi Barrani B3010 (3VP), Sollum B3610 (2VP), Bardia B4010 (3VP), Tobruk B4210 (5VP), Derna B4810 (3VP), Benghazi B5010 (5VP). Each turn spent idle is a wasted turn. Speed wins campaigns.

Prioritize capturing high-VP objectives: Tobruk (5VP) and Benghazi (5VP) are the biggest prizes. Bardia (3VP) and Derna (3VP) are on the way. Move the full combat stack along the coast road — splitting forces is unnecessary when the enemy is broken.

Italian units start with only 200 tons at Sidi Barrani depot. Water consumption is 1 ton/unit/turn. With 10 units, the depot runs dry by GT20. Plan for this: retreat toward Sollum (port) early, draw_from_supply_pool at ports, and create forward water dumps. Water death kills more Italians than Commonwealth guns.

When withdrawing, fall back to fortified hexes: Sollum (fort level 1), Bardia (fort level 2), Tobruk (fort level 3). Forts provide defensive bonuses that multiply effective strength. Fighting at Tobruk fort at 1:1 is equivalent to fighting in the open at 3:1.

When advancing along the coast road, leapfrog supply dumps: HQ creates dump at current position, combat units draw and advance 2-3 hexes, HQ advances and creates new dump. Capture enemy ports (Sidi Barrani, Sollum, Bardia) to shorten supply lines.
